dedupe_keys.name: nifc national wildland fire statistics fires acres and suppression costs since 1983

description: These tables give national statistics on wildland fires in the United States and on federal spending to suppress them. They are published by the National Interagency Fire Center, drawing on the Incident Management Situation Report of the National Interagency Coordination Center. The statistics pages give the total number of wildfires and acres burned each year from 1983 to 2025, federal suppression costs by year from 1985 split between the Forest Service and the Department of the Interior agencies, human-caused and lightning-caused fires by state, and incursions of unmanned aircraft into fire areas, plus current figures such as large fires being suppressed and personnel assigned. Annual reports and year-end statistics are downloadable for 2008 onwards. Coverage is national, with some tables by state or geographic area. Data are free as web tables and PDF reports from a federal source and are public domain. Caveats: early years are less complete, cost figures are nominal and cover federal suppression only, and state totals depend on agency reporting. Simulation uses: annual demand and cost series for sizing wildland firefighting resources and for validating wildfire emergency response models. Related records: the WFIGS incident locations (data-nifc-wfigs-wildland-fire-incident-locations) give incident-level records, and the fire occurrence database attributes (data-fpa-fod-attributes-us-wildfire-ignitions) give ignition points.
